Company secretary requirements in Malaysia: a guide for Sdn Bhd owners

Every Malaysian company needs a company secretary. Here is who qualifies, when you must appoint one and what they do.

By CCM Secretarial · Updated 30 September 2026

Is a company secretary compulsory in Malaysia?

Yes. Under the Companies Act 2016, every company incorporated in Malaysia — a Sdn Bhd, a public company or a company limited by guarantee — must have at least one company secretary. The company must appoint the first secretary within 30 days of incorporation. If the secretary leaves, the company must fill the vacancy within the period set by the Act.

Who can be a company secretary?

The secretary must be a natural person who ordinarily resides in Malaysia and is one of the following:

  • A member of a prescribed professional body, such as the Malaysian Institute of Accountants or the Malaysian Bar;
  • A person licensed by SSM as a company secretary; or
  • Another person approved by SSM.

Practically, most SMEs appoint a licensed company secretary from an outsourced firm, because the filing work is specialised and ongoing.

What does a company secretary actually do?

  • Lodges your annual return and financial statements with SSM on time;
  • Prepares and keeps minutes of board and general meetings;
  • Maintains statutory registers (directors, members, charges);
  • Files notices of changes — directors, share transfers, registered address;
  • Advises directors on their statutory duties and company law compliance.

What if you don’t appoint one?

Failing to have a company secretary is an offence under the Act and can result in compounds or penalties for the company and its officers, and it makes every other filing harder. If your company already missed the 30-day window, appoint a licensed secretary now and have them review outstanding filings.

FAQ

Quick answers

Can a director be the company secretary?

Yes, a director can also be the company secretary if they meet the qualification requirements in the Companies Act 2016. Many owners choose an outsourced secretary instead.

Can a foreigner be a company secretary in Malaysia?

The secretary must be a natural person ordinarily resident in Malaysia and qualified under the Act, so a non-resident cannot act.
